articles.title: Can Warriors survive without Stephen Curry with tough stretch ahead?
articles.summary: Off to a surprising start, Golden State must now deal with the loss of its leader in the short term.
articles.body:
On Thursday, the Golden State Warriors announced that star guard Steph Curry was diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be shelved for at least the next two weeks. The 38-year-old suffered the injury midway through the first quarter of Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets.

For a team and organization that has orbited around Curry's generational gravity for nearly two decades, the loss is significant. Prior to Wednesday's loss (Curry played just five minutes), he had been averaging near-identical production to his 2016 MVP season.

The 18-year veteran has been able to shoulder a seismic load — due to the absence of Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis' abrupt decision to step away from basketball citing health reasons — handling the ball more than ever and converting shots at the most efficient rate , all while minimizing turnovers. Curry has been the driving force for the 8-4 Warriors, who have won eight of their past nine games, which is nothing short of a testament to his greatness amid a loaded Western Conference and a team that, on paper, pales in comparison to its peers.

The Warriors' next seven games offer quite the challenge. In the coming fortnight, Golden State will face San Antonio, Dallas, Memphis, Boston and Portland, which have all won more than 60% of their games to date. But amid those upcoming hurdles, there's a strong belief within the locker room that the roster as-is can withstand Curry's absence in the short term.

"The spirit of this team is better," forward Draymond Green said to reporters following the game. "We're more certain of who we are, what makes us a good team. That puts us in a better position to be successful without him as opposed to where we were last year."

Green's assessment checks out. In 317 non-Curry minutes, the Warriors have been able to outscore teams by 14 points, according to PBP Stats, a substantial improvement from last season (Golden State lost those minutes by a whopping 135 points). The improvement of fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski, who will now come into focus as the team's biggest perimeter threat, will be tested in the interim. Albeit in a much-smaller role alongside Curry, Podziemski has been able to clean up his shot profile and ball security, two areas of focus for him since he was drafted in 2023. This season, Podz has taken on a much larger playmaking role when Curry is off the floor and is able to draw more fouls — in addition to excelling in transition and off-ball activity .

There's also the presence of rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, a Swiss Army knife of a combo forward that is equal parts thrilling and chaotic, who has taken on enough responsibility early on and converted his chances at veteran-level clips, currently in the 87th percentile of rim success and 79th in perimeter success, according to Cleaning the Glass. The first-year phenom is the team's second-leading scorer, averaging 21.7 points per game.

If the Warriors are to survive these next two weeks, they'll need to further emphasize their unselfish identity. Without Curry's gravity, ball movement becomes even more of a premium. They're second in passes made, third in assists and first in secondary assists because of a starting lineup that possesses five players who can create with the ball in their hands to varying degrees (Lendeborg, Podziemski, Al Horford, Draymond Green and the insertion of De'Anthony Melton, who likely picks up the minutes void and is a capable creator on his own).

(Melton's presence also juices the Warriors' penchant for forcing turnovers. They're surprisingly ninth in half-court defensive efficiency, fifth in opponent turnover rate and are good at turning mistakes into points, eighth-best at the time of this writing .)

The most important factor, however, during this period of uncertainty, is the leadership structure between Green and Kerr. Those two and Curry have been the lone constants over the years, and with Curry gone, Green and Kerr should be the consistent go-tos for guidance and morale.

They share a deep understanding and longevity that transcend most partnerships in sports. And they aren't new to uncomfortable situations — whether it's internal drama, injuries, or the growing pains that come with two-timeline situations.

"I was thrilled that the guys stayed together," Kerr said after Wednesday's game. "It's a great group to coach. I really love this team and I'm excited about what's ahead."

Make no mistake, Curry's absence, even if it's for two weeks, will be felt every time this team steps on the floor. But the energy about this new group, despite the lack of outside expectations, is tangible and might just be enough to hold down the fort until 30 is ready to go again.

articles.title: “Forgot to Tell Him I Love Him”: Prayers Pour In From Shaquille O’Neal While Mourning Deceased LSU Coach Dale Brown
articles.summary: In 1985, Dale Brown walked into an army base in West Germany and mistook a 13-year-old for a soldier. This interaction sparked a father-son bond that lasted...
articles.body:
In 1985, Dale Brown walked into an army base in West Germany and mistook a 13-year-old for a soldier. This interaction sparked a father-son bond that lasted more than four decades. It made saying goodbye an emotional affair for Shaquille O'Neal , after the legendary LSU coach passed away at 90. Standing before mourners, Shaq turned his grief into an earnest plea.

Speaking during Brown's Celebration of Life at LSU's Pete Maravich Assembly Center – nearly three weeks after the 448-game winner passed away on October 23 – O'Neal urged fans not to put off reaching out to the people they love. Battling through his emotions, Shaq recalled two prior incidents when he was too late.

"If you have a person you haven't talked to, that you haven't seen. Make sure you reach out. Because for me, this is the third time this has happened to me," O'Neal said .

"My sister passed away, and I forgot to tell her I love her. Kobe Bryant passed away, I forgot to tell him I love him. And now my daddy Dale is gone, and I forgot to tell him I love him."

Brown was more than just a simple coach to Shaq. He was the person who helped O'Neal discover his talent and helped foster it when Shaq didn't believe in himself.

When Brown first met O'Neal at the military base in West Germany, the future NBA superstar was already 6-foot-9 at just 13 years old.

However, Shaq lacked confidence in his abilities and even considered following his stepfather into the Army. Brown saw something different in the towering teenager and immediately took an interest in his future. He stubbornly advised Shaq through it all.

The LSU coach began writing to O'Neal every week, sharing basketball advice and encouragement. This tradition continued even after Shaq returned to the United States. When Shaq was at his lowest, Brown continued to advise him and eventually offered him a scholarship to play basketball at LSU.

Recalling that life-changing first meeting, O'Neal once said, "He put his arms around me like he found gold." It wasn't a small gesture; that one moment changed the course of Shaq's life.

At Brown's Celebration of Life, O'Neal summed up the significance of Brown's guidance.

"He was the first person in my life who believed in me."

Playing under Brown at LSU helped shape O'Neal into one of the most dominant college basketball players and a top center. During those three college years, he showed continuous development.

He averaged 13.9ppg, 12rpg and 3.6 blocks per game as a freshman, 27.6ppg, 14.7rpg and 5 blocks per game as a sophomore, and 24.1ppg, 14rpg, and 5.2 blocks per game as a junior.

O'Neal entered the 1992 draft as the unanimous top player and was selected No. 1 overall. From there, Shaq's star only continued to rise, winning four NBA championships and cementing himself as one of the greatest centers of all time.

His relationship with Brown didn't end after he entered the NBA. In fact, Shaq continued to describe Brown as a father figure years into his NBA career. In a letter he wrote to Brown in 1999, Shaq made that abundantly clear.

"You are one of my heroes, one of my idol, one of my good friends," O'Neal wrote, according to the LSU website.

And while Brown's legacy at LSU is defined by much more than his relationship with Shaq, the numbers tell their own story. Across 25 seasons as head coach from 1972 to 1997, he recorded a school-best 448 victories, led the Tigers to two Final Four appearances and won four SEC regular-season championships. He also coached several notable players, including Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf and O'Neal.

For Shaq, however, one personal regret remained. Despite everything he achieved under Brown's guidance and the decades of friendship that followed, he wished he had told his mentor how much he loved him before it was too late.

To O'Neal, the legendary coach would always be "Daddy Dale." His final plea was not about basketball, championships, or fame. It was a reminder for people to share love with the ones who shaped their lives while they still can.

articles.title: Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson to undergo surgery on hand, reportedly out 4-6 weeks
articles.summary: Wilson fractured his right hand during Chicago's loss to the Spurs on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls will reportedly be without rookie Caleb Wilson for a while. After suffering a fractured right hand on Wednesday, Wilson is set to undergo surgery and will miss four to six weeks, per multiple reports.

Wilson suffered the injury during the second half of Wednesday's loss to the San Antonio Spurs, heading to the locker room in the third quarter. He was ruled out of the game before the start of the fourth quarter.

It was unclear when Wilson sustained the fractured, though the Bulls broadcast highlighted a play where Wilson's right hand got jammed against Victor Wembanyama's elbow.

Wilson, who was selected No. 4 overall out of North Carolina in June, was touted as a young player to help revive the Bulls. A dominant showing in the NBA Summer League boosted Wilson's profile ahead of the regular season.

So far, he has shown a lot of promise, averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game as a starting power forward.

However, Wilson has a history of hand injuries, fracturing each of his hands — his left hand in February and his right hand in March before the NCAA tournament — during his lone freshman season with the Tar Heels.

articles.title: El Real Madrid revienta otra caja fuerte
articles.standfirst: Los blancos destrozan a la mejor defensa de la Euroliga con grandes actuaciones de Feliz (11+4+7) y de jugadores necesitados: Luwawu-Cabarrot (22), Procida (19), Smith (13) y Sarr
articles.summary: Los blancos destrozan a la mejor defensa de la Euroliga con grandes actuaciones de Feliz (11+4+7) y de jugadores necesitados: Luwawu-Cabarrot (22), Procida (19), Smith (13) y Sarr
articles.body: En los últimos tres partidos de la Euroliga, el Real Madrid se ha medido a tres de las mejores defensas de la competición: Fenerbahce, Panathinaikos y Estrella Roja. Las ha dinamitado todas, aunque contra los griegos no le diera para ganar. Los serbios llegaban con los mejores registros defensivos y salieron hechos escombros (105-84). Recibían 74 puntos de media y ya habían encajado esa cifra a falta de 17 minutos y más de la mitad de ellos (38) en el primer cuarto. Los blancos reventaron otra caja fuerte y el plan de Ibon Navarro. Sensacional partido del Madrid, que sólo se fue del partido durante siete minutos del segundo cuarto. Dominio absoluto el resto del tiempo con monopolio del rebote durante muchos minutos y grandes porcentajes: 16/25 en tiros de dos, 17/36 en triples y un solo tiro libre fallado de 23 intentos. Y, ante la acumulación de bajas (Campazzo, Maledon, Deck, Jantunen y Garuba), buenas actuaciones de quienes más lo necesitaban. Procida hizo 19 puntos con 4/5 triples; Smith, tras unos partidos a cero, batió su tope anotador en la Euroliga con 13; el ciclotímico Luwawu-Cabarrot tuvo el día bueno con 22; Sarr, cada vez mejor, cumplió de ‘4’ y de ‘5’; y completísimo Feliz, con 11 puntos, siete asistencias y cuatro rebotes, de nuevo como único base puro. El Madrid fue un huracán en el inicio que se llevó por delante al Estrella Roja y a su rocosa defensa. Procida, con 10 puntos sin fallo, soplaba más que nadie. Triple, rebote ofensivo, mate... Sacó todo el muestrario para poner el 19-9. Cuando mejor estaba, se fue al banquillo sustituido por Luwawu-Cabarrot, que le tomó el relevo anotador. Ocho puntos seguidos para mantener a su equipo en órbita. Un 2+1 de Okeke cerró un primer cuarto bestial de los blancos (38-20). Apabullaron en el rebote (12-1), no fallaron un tiro de dos (9/9) y anularon todos los recursos ofensivos de su rival. Un triple de Procida y otro de Feliz al inicio del segundo periodo (6/11) pusieron una máxima por entonces de 24 puntos (44-20), pero ahí llegó la pájara local. El Estrella Roja había aprendido a rebotear, al Madrid ya no le entraban los triples e iba acumulando pérdidas. Encajó un parcial de 2-19 con un estelar Tyson Carter (46-39), que se fue al banquillo con tres faltas, la segunda de ellas inexistente. Los serbios acusaron su salida de la pista. Después de siete minutos malviviendo con cuatro tiros libres, Pradilla metió un triple para los blancos. Fue el inicio de un 8-0 en apenas 45 segundos. Al descanso, se estiraba de nuevo el marcador: 56-41. El Madrid recuperó su identidad en la reanudación y dejó las cosas claras con un parcial de 14-6 a lomos de Feliz (70-47). Ya no hubo reacción pese al despertar de Nwora en los visitantes y los triples de Baldwin. Un motivado Smith, al que el Palacio reconoció sus ganas, cerró el tercer cuarto en 82-59. Las rentas pasaron de los 30 con un triple de Abalde (92-61). “El Madrid te mete 100 puntos sin querer”, decía Ibon Navarro a MARCA en la previa. Ahí quedaron: 105. Y porque el triple final de Okeke desde 20 metros no entró en tiempo. 105 - Real Madrid (38+18+26+23): Feliz (11), Smith Jr (13), Procida (19), Pradilla (5) y Tavares (4) -cinco inicial-, Shulga (-), Abalde (8), Okeke (9), Luwawu-Cabarrot (22), Llull (7), Jones (-) y Sarr (7). 84 - Estrella Roja (20+21+18+25): Jones (8), Carter (18), Nwora (12), Moneke (3) y Koloko (4) -cinco inicial-, Weiler-Babb (2), Butler (2), Davidovic (5), Dobric (9), Baldwin Jr (11), Ojeleye (5) y Krämer (5). Árbitros: Robert Lottermoser (Alemania), Kristaps Konstantinovs (Letonia) y Rain Peerandi (Estonia). Señalaron falta técnica a Ibon Navarro (min.4), entrenador del Estrella Roja. Sin eliminados. articles.title: Spurs add De'Aaron Fox to injury list ahead of NBA Cup game against Warriors
articles.summary: The hottest team in the NBA could be without two starters in Fox and Devin Vassell when it hosts Golden State on Friday in an NBA Cup group stage game.
articles.body:
The Spurs could be without two starters when they host the Golden State Warriors on Friday night.

The hottest team in the NBA listed guard De'Aaron Fox (left hip soreness) and forward Devin Vassell (left adductor tightness) as questionable for the first of three meetings between the teams this season.

The Spurs will also be without forward Tobias Harris, who has yet to play this season after suffering a left calf strain early in training camp.

Vassell has missed the last two games. The Spurs added Fox to the injury report after he had 17 points, nine assists, four rebounds and three steals in 31 minutes of the 124-119 come-from-behind win at Chicago on Wednesday night.

The Spurs (10-2) rallied from a 22-point second quarter deficit to record their 10th win in a row.

The Warriors (8-4) also have injury concerns after they announced Thursday that Stephen Curry has an oblique abdominal tear that will sideline him for at least two weeks if not longer.

Charles Bassey, who played three seasons for the Spurs from 2022-2025 after performing as a prep star at St. Anthony in San Antonio, is probable with left toe soreness.

The game is set for 8:30 p.m. and is scheduled to be televised nationally on Prime. It's the Spurs' second NBA Cup group stage game after it defeated the Kings last Friday in Sacramento.

The NBA suspended the Houston Rockets guard without pay on Thursday after swinging at, then grazing, Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey. Smart and Bassey got tied up fighting for position under the glass, barked at each other trailing the play, and Smart uncorked a right hook that grazed Bassey's nose. articles.title: No. 2 UConn defeats No. 17 Ohio State in Columbus with Sarah Strong scoring 25 points in 87-55 win
articles.summary: Strong scored 20 points in the second half  for the Huskies after sitting out the entire second quarter with foul trouble.
articles.body:
The UConn women's basketball team has won two consecutive games versus Big Ten competition since losing at Michigan a week ago .

Visiting Columbus, the Huskies defeated No. 17 Ohio State 87-55 on Thursday. Sarah Strong followed up her career-best performance in Sunday's win over Iowa with 25 points, 20 in the second half. In addition to making 7 of 8 3-pointers, she tallied 9 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals.

Ashlynn Shade added 15 points, while KK Arnold scored 10 points with 5 assists and 5 steals. The Huskies pulled away in the fourth quarter with bench production, getting 9 points from Kelis Fisher, 8 from Allie Ziebell and Olivia Vukosa getting 8 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists and 2 blocks.

UConn put Ohio State back on its heels from the opening tip with Ashlynn Shade swishing her first 3-point attempt. That began a 12-2 run for the Huskies.

The lead increased to 21-8 before Ohio State pushed back with a 10-2 surge to end the first quarter. The Buckeyes' run was aided by the Huskies' turnovers, which irritated head coach Geno Auriemma.

Strong was also limited by early foul trouble, sitting down after drawing her second foul nine minutes into the game. She sat out the entire second quarter, scoring only five points.

Neither team shot well in the second quarter, combining for a total of six points midway through the frame. UConn went ahead 33-25 on a midrange jumper from Kayleigh Heckel, but Ohio State followed that up with Ava Watson scoring eight points to cut the Huskies' lead to two points. The Huskies had a chance to take a five-point margin into halftime, but Jana El Alfy's layup went in after the buzzer.

Strong aggressively looked for her shot in the third quarter, hitting three 3-pointers. The third of those long-range shots pushed UConn's lead back up to 10 points. That came after what could have been a game-turning development for Ohio State.

Following a turnover, Huskies center Olivia Vukosa was called for a flagrant 1 foul for swinging her arm and hitting Kennedy Cambridge. Watson made one of her two free throws, but Jaloni Cambridge missed a 3 on the ensuing possession and UConn scored the next five points.

Cambridge led the Buckeyes with 21 points, 6 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 steals. Watson was the only other Buckeye to score in double figures, tallying 13 points. Kennedy Cambridge added seven assists and four steals to go with her eight points. However, the Buckeyes shot 35% (19 for 55) from the floor, going 5 for 24 on 3-pointers.

UConn moves on to ACC competition for its next matchup, visiting No. 7 Louisville on Sunday. Ohio State hosts Fairleigh Dickinson on Sunday before two games against SEC opponents, hosting No. 21 Ole Miss and facing No. 6 Texas in Fort Worth.

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert Updates Search for New WNBA Commissioner, Gives Timeline for Hire
articles.summary: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert revealed that the search for the league's new commissioner is an "ongoing process" on Thursday, according to Annie Costabile of The Athletic.
articles.body:
WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert revealed that the search for the league's new commissioner is an "ongoing process" on Thursday, according to Annie Costabile of The Athletic.

Engelbert was hopeful that a new commissioner would be hired by Dec. 31 after the league started meeting with candidates in person over the past two weeks, per Costabile.

On Sept. 4, Engelbert announced that she would be retiring from her position at the end of the year.

She initially took over the role in 2019.

While the exact candidates for the upcoming vacancy are unknown, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum is a possible option. Tatum previously served as the WNBA's interim president from 2018-19 and could take on an interim commissioner role if Engelbert's replacement isn't found by the end of the year, per Costabile.

The WNBA is coming off a 2026 season in which it reached 90 million unique viewers across all national networks during the regular season, setting a new record .

The league also set records for total and average attendance, drawing 3.8 million fans in the regular season to go along with an average attendance of 11,474 fans per game.

Engelbert's tenure as commissioner still wasn't perfect, as she drew criticism from multiple players during collective bargaining agreement negotiations in 2025.

Now, the WNBA appears to be making progress in the search for its next commissioner.

articles.title: Maxey Leads 76ers Past Raptors, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Embiid, Top Players with LeBron Out
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers were without LeBron James on Thursday night due to lower back/sciatica management. It didn't keep Philly from picking up its 10th win of the season.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers were without LeBron James on Thursday night due to lower back/sciatica management. It didn't keep Philly from picking up its 10th win of the season.

The Sixers overcame the absence of James and a slow start, beating the Toronto Raptors 123-112.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

Philly got off to a rough start, finding themselves in a 32-16 hole in the first quarter. But the Sixers answered with a 15-0 run to get back into the game, outscored Toronto by a 36-27 margin in both the second and third quarters each and ultimately pulled away from Toronto.

As usual, Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers' star-studded offense, though it was truly a balanced affair from the starting unit:

It didn't hurt that Anfernee Simons, Jabari Walker and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope shot a combined 9-for-13 from three off the bench.

It all spoiled a fantastic night from RJ Barrett, who had to pick up the slack with no Scottie Barnes or Kawhi Leonard in the lineup and did his part.

But it wasn't enough to get past the 10-3 Sixers, who continue to impress early in the 2026-27 season. Up next for Philly is a Sunday showdown against the Indiana Pacers.

The Raptors (5-7) will lick their wounds after a third straight loss, hoping to end the streak against the New York Knicks on Sunday.

articles.title: New WNBA Rumors on 2027 Season Schedule Reveal Start, End Dates for Record 50-Game Campaign
articles.summary: The 2027 WNBA season, which will feature 50 games for the first time in league history, is reportedly expected to begin on Thursday, May 7, per ESPN's Alexa Philippou.
articles.body:
The 2027 WNBA season, which will feature 50 games for the first time in league history, is reportedly expected to begin on Thursday, May 7, per ESPN's Alexa Philippou .

The latest possible end date (should the WNBA Finals go a full seven games) is Saturday, Oct. 24.

The WNBA's regular season slate increased from 36 games in 2022 to 40 games in 2023 and 2024, and then 44 contests in 2025 and 2026.

Now it'll rise by six more. Per Philippou, the collective bargaining agreement allows a maximum of 50 games in 2027 and 2028, and 52 beginning in 2029.

The postseason matchups have expanded in recent years as well. Of note, the WNBA Finals is best-of-seven as of 2025, and single-elimination rounds were removed following the 2021 campaign.

The 2027 season won't feature a midseason break for international competition, à la 2024 (Summer Olympics) or 2026 (FIBA World Cup). Last season ran from May 8 to October 31, when the Golden State Valkyries — led by Gabby Williams' 30 points — ended their seven-game WNBA Finals win over the Atlanta Dream with a 68-63 victory.

The next WNBA season also won't feature any new expansion teams, but that will change in 2028, when the Cleveland Sirens begin play to round out the league with 16 teams. Detroit (2029) and Philadelphia (2030) will join within the next few years.

articles.title: Joel Embiid scores 20 in 76ers' win over Raptors after knee injury scare; LeBron James sat out for back management
articles.summary: Both James and Embiid have missed two of the 76ers' 12 games this season.
articles.body:
After being listed as questionable up until game time, Joel Embiid scored 20 points in the Philadelphia 76ers' 123-112 win over the Toronto Raptors on Thursday.

Embiid also avoided what initially appeared to be a knee injury early in the first quarter when Ja'Kobe Walter ran into him trying to avoid a screen. Walter's right knee collided with Embiid's right knee, sending the center to the floor. Embiid pointed to his knee as trainers came out to check him, causing fears that he may have been seriously hurt.

However, Embiid re-entered the game three minutes later and scored his first basket with under two minutes remaining in the first quarter.

Up until a half-hour before tip-off, Embiid was listed on the injury report as questionable with "right foot plantar fascia injury management." That had also sidelined him for two of the Sixers' game in the early season.

"I have no idea," Embiid said when asked by ESPN's Kris Rhim during shootaround if he was playing versus the Raptors. "We'll see what they have to say and then we'll go from there."

Tyrese Maxey scored 27 to lead the Sixers, also dishing out 8 assists. Jaylen Brown added 18 with 6 rebounds, Anfernee Simons contributed 17 points (hitting 5-of-6 3-pointers) off the bench and VJ Edgecombe finished with 15 points, 8 board, 8 assists and 3 steals. Philadelphia improved its record to 9-3, 5-2 at home.

For the Raptors, RJ Barrett led all scorers with 31 points (shooting 4-for-7 on 3s) in addition to 14 rebounds and 5 assists. Immanuel Quickley added 26 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists. Collin Murray-Boyles scored 14 points with 4 assists and 5 blocks. Toronto dropped to 5-7 (3-4 on the road) with the defeat.

While Embiid played, LeBron James sat out his third game of the early 2026-27 season on Thursday. James was listed on the Sixers' injury report as out with "low back/sciatica management," which had been the reason he's sat two of Philadelphia's previous 12 games this season.

The 41-year-old was listed as questionable until participating in Thursday's shootaround. He was then downgraded.

Thursday's game was not part of a back-to-back for the 76ers, so that was not a consideration in sitting James and possibly resting Embiid. Philadelphia last played on Tuesday, losing 123-101 to the Boston Celtics in the hyped first meeting between former teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum.

However, the Sixers do play back-to-back games on Sunday and Monday, hosting the Indiana Pacers then visiting the Brooklyn Nets.

So far this season, James is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.5 assists on 43% shooting from the floor. Embiid is scoring 17.7 points per game with 9.3 rebounds and 3.8 assists. He is also shooting 37%, while making only 4 of 33 (12%) 3-point attempts.

Without Embiid, Philadelphia would have been short-handed at center with Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction) also out for Thursday. Perhaps that influenced the decision to play him against the Raptors.

James started at center when Embiid was sidelined on Oct. 25 versus the Detroit Pistons. Had Embiid been out, the Sixers would have faced going small with 6-foot-7 Jabari Walker in the middle (who subbed in when Embiid left the game), or perhaps played 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall for only the second time this season. Fall played one minute in Thursday's win.

Led by a stellar performance from LaMelo Ball, the Minnesota Timberwolves cruised to a 133-94 win over the Dallas Mavericks at the Target Center on Thursday night.

The contest didn't initially seem as if it would become so one-sided, as Dallas took a 24-19 lead late in the first quarter.

Minnesota ended the quarter on a 15-2 run that was capped off by a buzzer-beating triple from Jaylen Clark, though.

Adebayo had a simpler take: “I feel like Vice City has its own fashion culture.”Jennifer Alvarez, the Heat’s chief creative officer, said the team is “bringing sports and entertainment together in a way that’s never been done.” The idea started in December 2023, when Rockstar’s trailer showed a digital Kaseya Center in its first 30 seconds. Miami has leaned on the Vice name since 2017 and has released five earlier Vice jerseys. Alvarez said this one feels like the payoff of all of them.Kaseya Center gets a full Vice City makeoverA “Welcome to Vice City” sign is going up on the arena roof. Fans can already order from Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell, two fast-food chains from the series. articles.title: Cade Cunningham Makes History as Pistons Beat Wizards, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Trae, More
articles.summary: Cade Cunningham's historic night powered the Detroit Pistons to a 144-140 win over the Washington Wizards in double overtime on Thursday.
articles.body:
Cade Cunningham's historic night powered the Detroit Pistons to a 144-140 win over the Washington Wizards in double overtime on Thursday.

Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points in the victory.

He also dished out 11 assists, becoming the first player to record at least 50 points and 10 assists without committing a turnover since the 1977-78 season.

Meanwhile, Washington became the first NBA team to lose a game in which three players scored at least 30 points since the Oklahoma City Thunder in 2023.

Here's a closer look at how Cunningham as well as Wizards stars Trae Young and Anthony Davis fared during the contest:

The game was a hard-fought battle that featured 13 ties and 20 lead changes.

Neither team led by more than 11 points during the contest.

Detroit gained a 121-118 edge before the end of regulation due to a pair of free throws by Cunningham, although Young sent the game to overtime with a buzzer-beating three.

Washington opened overtime on a 7-0 run, although the Pistons immediately responded with an 11-2 run of their own to move back in front.

Still, the Wizards forced double overtime after rookie AJ Dybantsa connected on a pull-up jumper at the free throw line.

Both teams continued to battle in the second overtime period before Detroit gained a late two-point lead.

With just under 30 seconds remaining, Cunningham buried a fadeaway jump shot from the baseline to give the Pistons a four-point advantage that they ultimately wouldn't relinquish.

Cunningham shot 64.0 percent from the field and 60.0 percent from three-point territory while the rest of Detroit's lineup connected on 44.6 percent of its field goals and 33.3 percent of its triples.

The Pistons improved to 8-3 with the win.

articles.title: Commanders-Giants: Cam Skattebo refuses to be normal, stares into camera during 'Thursday Night Football'
articles.summary: NFL fans were treated to a haunting sight in the fourth quarter of Commanders-Giants.
articles.body:
The fourth quarter of the Washington Commanders' dramatic 24-21 victory over the New York Giants Thursday began with a haunting sight for the folks at home.

Giants running back Cam Skattebo, never one for walking the beaten path, spent at least 10 seconds staring down the Prime Video cameras for reasons known only to him. Prime's Al Michaels was at least entertained, laughing and remarking, "He knows where the camera is."

Skattebo finished with 78 rushing yards, 44 receiving yards and two rushing touchdowns, so he also did this during a fairly productive game.

Up until that point, we thought the oddest thing about Skattebo's night would have been him breaking into laughter after throwing up on the sideline. He explained after the game he had eaten a pretzel-wrapped hot dog before the game that didn't sit well.

Skattebo was something of a question mark entering Thursday after sustaining a hamstring tear in Week 7, forcing him to miss the Giants' win over the Philadelphia Eagles last week.

In his first seven games of the season, the former fourth-round pick had 418 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns and 76 receiving yards. He doubled that touchdown total on Thursday.

articles.title: Cade Cunningham scores career-high 52 points in Pistons' 144-140 win in 2OT over Wizards
articles.summary: Cunningham became the first NBA player to score 50-plus points with 10-plus assists and no turnovers since turnovers were first recorded in 1977.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham became the first NBA player to record 50 or more points with 10-plus assists and no turnovers in a 144-140 win over the Washington Wizards in double overtime on Thursday.

Turnovers weren't officially recorded by the NBA until 1977 , so it isn't certain that Cunningham is the first player to ever post that stat line. However, only three players in the past 49 years — Michael Jordan, Nikola Jokić and Damian Lillard — had scored 50 with 10 assists and 1 turnover. ( Hat tip to Yahoo Sports' Dan Devine for that factoid.)

Cunningham finished with a career-high 52 points, shooting 16-of-25 from the floor (including 3-for-5 on 3-pointers) and making 17 of 18 free throws in Detroit's win.

Washington (4-9) lost despite three players scoring 30 or more points. Trae Young tallied 37 points with 14 assists, while both Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr added 30 points. Davis also grabbed 15 rebounds and Sarr added nine. The Wizards have lost six consecutive games, including two of their past three to the Pistons.

The Pistons and Wizards played a close game throughout regulation, trading the lead back and forth during the fourth quarter.

With 1.8 seconds left in regulation out of a timeout, Young caught the ball on the right wing and hit a game-tying 3-pointer with two players defending him. It was 121-121.

Pistons head coach J.B. Bickerstaff was not happy about allowing Young's shot, saying "we didn't pay attention to the details."

"We hold ourselves to a higher standard," he added. "In certain moments when we have to be able to generate a stop, we gotta be able to trust each other."

In the first overtime, the Wizards ran out to a 130-121 lead capped by a Sarr dunk off a lob from Davis. From there, the Pistons went on an 11-2 run — with seven points from Cunningham — to go back on top. Yet Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa hit a jumper from the free-throw line to extend the game to another overtime.

A 3-pointer by Cunningham gave Detroit the advantage in the second overtime, a narrow lead the Pistons held until 1:10 remaining when Bilal Coulibaly tied the score at 140-140 on a dunk. Yet Cunningham put the Pistons ahead for good on a midrange jumper with 25 seconds remaining. Two Kevin Huerter free throws gave Detroit its final four-point margin.

"To be able to do what he does in the moment, when it's called on, it's unique and special," Bickerstaff said of Cunningham . "He never ceases to amaze. He just understands what it takes to get it done and has all the abilities to make those things happen."

Daniss Jenkins added 21 points for the Pistons (8-3). Thompson recorded his first career triple-double with 17 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists, along with 3 steals and 3 blocks.

articles.title: Cade Cunningham logra lo nunca visto en la NBA: 52 puntos y 11 asistencias sin mácula de pérdidas
articles.standfirst: Primer jugador en la historia de la NBA en lograr con 50 puntos, 10 asistencias y 0 pérdidas de balón en un partido
articles.summary: Primer jugador en la historia de la NBA en lograr con 50 puntos, 10 asistencias y 0 pérdidas de balón en un partido
articles.body: Cade Cunningham se ha convertido en el primer jugador en la historia de la NBA en lograr con 50 puntos, 10 asistencias y 0 pérdidas de balón en un partido, desde que se empezaron a registrar las pérdidas de balón individuales en la temporada 1977-78. La estrella de los Pistons firmó 52 puntos y 11 asistencias en la victoria de los Pistons ante los Wizards por 140-144 tras dos prórrogas. En un encuentro que se mantuvo muy reñido durante casi todo su desarrollo, Cunningham minimizó sus errores y, al mismo tiempo, mantuvo un nivel de productividad extraordinario. "Sin duda, ha sido la mejor actuación de mi carrera en la NBA", reconoció Cunningham, base de 1,98 m. y 25 años que fue el número 1 del Draft en 2021. Cunningham igualó la cuarta mayor anotación individual en la historia de la franquicia de los Pistons. Jerry Stackhouse anotó 57 puntos en un partido de 2001, Kelly Tripucka sumó 56 en 1983, Dave Bing alcanzó los 54 en 1971 y George Yardley anotó 52 en 1958. "Cade Cunningham nos guio a través del último cuarto y las prórrogas. Hizo lo que suele hacer. No basta con que un solo jugador intente defenderlo" declaró Ausar Thompson, que logró un triple-doble de 17 puntos, 11 asistencias y 11 rebotes. Cade Cunningham también se convirtió en el quinto jugador en registrar un 'doble-doble' de 50 puntos sin cometer ninguna pérdida de balón en un partido desde la temporada 1977-78, uniéndose a Michael Jordan (en dos ocasiones), Moses Malone, Carmelo Anthony y Giannis Antetokounmpo. Otros de sus records en una noche mágica fueron que convirtió en el tercer jugador de los Pistons en lograr un 'doble-doble'de 50 puntos, uniéndose a Yardley (quien lo hizo dos veces en la temporada 1957-58) y a Blake Griffin (en la 2018-19), y que anotó 30 puntos entre el último cuarto y la prórroga, la mayor cantidad registrada por un jugador de los Pistons en la era de los registros detallados jugada a jugada (desde la temporada 1997-98). En este partido participaron cuatro jugadores que fueron elegidos como números 1 del Draft NBA: Dybantsa, Anthony Davis (30 puntos y 15 rebotes), Deandre Ayton y Cunningham. Trae Young forzó la primera prórroga con un tiro sobre la bocina defendido por dos jugadores de los Pistons, y el novato AJ Dybantsa hizo lo propio cinco minutos de juego después, cuando anotó una suspensión desde el tiro libre para forzar un nuevo tiempo extra. Cunningham sentenció el partido en la segunda prórroga con un tiro desde el borde de la pintura que puso el 138-142 en el marcador a falta de 25 segundos Young anotó 37 puntos y Alex Sarr sumó 30 para los Wizards.

articles.title: NBA: Cunningham scores 52 as Pistons win double OT thriller against Wizards
articles.summary: Cunningham became the first NBA player to record a 50-point, 10-assist game without committing a turnover since 1977-78.
articles.body:
Cade Cunningham racked up 52 points as the Detroit Pistons edged a double-overtime thriller 144-140 against Washington on Thursday.

The Wizards twice extended the game with clutch scores in the dying seconds but could not repeat the trick a third time as the Pistons held their nerve to claim an epic road win.

Cunningham became the first player in NBA history to score 50 points and add 10 assists with zero turnovers, while Ausar Thompson had a triple-double with 17 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds.

The Wizards had three starters scoring 30-plus points – Trae Young, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr – but it was not enough to prevent Washington’s sixth defeat in a row.

“Two overtimes, it was just going to come down [to] who wanted it more, who had more in the tank,” said Cunningham.

“I’d bet on my team any day. So great win for us.”

In a back-and-forth game featuring 20 lead changes, Detroit started slow but built a double-digit lead early in the second half.

It was slowly whittled down by Washington, but the Pistons were clinging to their lead when Cunningham was fouled at 119-118 with less than two seconds remaining.

Cunningham sank both free throws, but Trae Young made a nerveless try right at the buzzer to force overtime.

The Wizards raced 128-121 up, but Cunningham would not quit.

He made a three-pointer with 30 seconds left to level the score, then set up Duncan Robinson for what appeared to be another. A video replay ruled Robinson’s toe was on the line, and Detroit had only a two-point lead.

That proved crucial as Young set up this year’s top draft pick AJ Dybantsa , who forced a second overtime period with a pull-up jump shot.

Cunningham made a fadeaway shot for a four-point lead with 25 seconds left, and this time the Wizards could not conjure a third comeback.

Young missed two three-point efforts, with Washington settling for two free throws, but unable to score in their final possession.

Tyrese Maxey powered Philadelphia to its latest comeback victory, scoring 27 points as the Sixers shrugged off a slow start and the absence of LeBron James to beat the Toronto Raptors 123-112.

Maxey added eight assists, linking up seamlessly with Joel Embiid, who briefly left the court early with a knee injury but returned to add 20 points.

The Sixers had trailed by 17 points in the first quarter, immediately following Embiid’s absence, but rallied for their fifth double-digit comeback this season.

“We’ll take it. I mean, extreme professional win by us. We stayed with it. Didn’t start out great, but it was a good win,” said Maxey.

“We played together the last seven years, so I kind of know where he’s going to be, he knows where I’m going to be at, and it’s good for us,” he said of his partnership with 2023 MVP Embiid.

Veteran James, who turns 42 next month, was ruled out of Thursday’s clash to manage a lower back issue.

Philadelphia moved to 10-3, just half a game back from the 10-2 Boston Celtics atop the Eastern Conference.

The Minnesota Timberwolves thrashed Dallas 133-94, while Devin Booker’s 30 points helped the Phoenix Suns overcome Charlotte 101-96.

articles.title: Hawks Are Hot, But The Eastern Conference Reality Check Is Here
articles.summary: The Hawks sit fourth in the East, but a loss to the Lakers exposed cracks. Can Atlanta survive the weak schedule while Dyson Daniels leads the way?
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks are sitting pretty at 7-5, but that record might be a bit of a mirage. Monday's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers ended their four-game winning streak, placing them fourth in the Eastern Conference. The team has had a solid start, yet the gap between looking good and being a real contender is wide. Sports Illustrated notes that the Hawks have played more games than any other league team so far, indicating a brutal schedule.

Staying in the upper echelon of the East currently requires winning against bad teams. With a combined 2-20 record, the Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks rank as two of the worst NBA teams. If the Hawks drop games against these bottom-tier squads, they will fall fast. To keep pace, Atlanta must take care of business against the worst of the bunch.

While the offense can be shaky, Dyson Daniels is doing something special on both ends of the floor. Although Jalen Johnson receives more hype, he is arguably Atlanta's most impactful player right now. Daniels just posted 10 points, eight rebounds, and six assists against the Lakers, along with four steals. For the whole season, he holds a team-best plus-58 rating when he is on the court. He is the Hawks' best defender, and without him, the mediocre defense would be much worse.

As the team prepares to face Chicago, he demonstrates high-level play as one of the NBA's most underrated impact players. Julius Okongwu has posted 16 or more points in each of his last three outings and recorded nine rebounds in four of his last five contests. He has a plus-38 rating in his minutes.

Not everyone is playing well, and Lu Dort is the biggest concern for the coaching staff. It has not been a great season for him in Atlanta, and the loss to the Lakers showed why. Dort scored only four points and shot 1-for-6 from three against the Lakers. He is a minus-38 in his minutes, the lowest on the entire team. When he does not shoot well, his defense is not good enough to justify the heavy minutes he is getting.

The center position is another headache. Jock Landale returned from injury but played only 14 minutes against the Lakers and finished with five points. It was a questionable move to play him over rookie Zuby Ejiofor, who only played 3:52. Landale was not exceptional in his time, and the backup minutes remain a puzzle for Quin Snyder. According to reports, the Hawks rank 16th in points allowed per 100 possessions, marking them as a middle-of-the-pack defense. If they lose to Chicago or Milwaukee, it will be because they could not stop the other team's offense.

Friday night will see the Hawks resume play on the road against the Chicago Bulls.

articles.summary: La selección puede conseguir la clasificación en las Ventanas y el seleccionador tirará por primera vez en noviembre de los internacionales de la Euroliga y seis invitados
articles.body: Situaciones trascendentales, medidas extraordinarias. Chus Mateo acaba de anunciar la convocatoria para las Ventanas FIBA de noviembre y, por primera vez, presentó una lista mixta, con jugadores de la Euroliga, que se incorporarán según acaben sus partidos de la máxima competición europea, previstos para martes 24 (Valencia, Barça y Panathinaikos) y miércoles 25 (Real Madrid y Anadolu Efes). Los encuentros en Podgorica (ante Montenegro, jueves 26 de noviembre) y Santiago de Compostela (frente a Grecia, domingo 29) pueden certificar la clasificación de la selección para el Mundial de Qatar 2027. Por eso, el seleccionador ha tirado de todo los recursos humanos disponibles, con una fórmula en la que aparecen los habituales del verano Brizuela, Parra, Pradilla, Juancho y Willy Hernángomez, Abalde, Yusta, Cárdenas y Saint-Supery y también las novedades como invitados de Alocén (Gran Canaria), que vuelve a una convocatoria desde Primera FEB, Sima y Alderete, y los estrenos de Pablo Tamba, Mikel Sanz y Adriá Torres. España podría clasificarse para lo que sería su presencia 14ª en la historia de la Copa del Mundo (20 ediciones). No falla desde la edición en Filipinas de 1978. Para ello, debe ganar los dos partidos o al menos el segundo, en Fontes do Sar, ante Grecia si supera el básket-average (-3) tras el encuentro disputado en Atenas en agosto. Después de las dos derrotas en las últimas Ventanas clasificatorias, la selección va segunda en el grupo I (5-3) por detrás de Ucrania (6-2). Georgia es tercera (5-3) y Portugal (4-4) y Grecia (4-4) aún cuentan con opciones de entrar en los tres primeros (que otorga el billete directo para Qatar) a falta de cuatro partidos, aunque el combinado heleno podría despedirse en estas mismas Ventanas en función de los resultados. El partido de Santiago es una finalísima para los helenos y también para España, de ahí la convocatoria con ocho jugadores de la Euroliga. Mateo, que deseó tener más jugadores españoles en la Liga Endesa para tener más donde elegir, explicó así la singularidad de la lista en estas fechas. "La situación competitiva ha cambiado. Es el mejor momento de hacerlo así porque hay una situación en la que necesitamos estar en el Mundial y queremos tener el mejor nivel posible. Los chicos desde el primer momento, viendo que la clasificación estaba apretada, me han pedido formar parte de ello. No les voy a dejar fuera si quieren representar a la selección. En esta ocasión, aunque siempre hemos respetado lo duro del calendario, hemos creído conveniente convocarlos. Nuestra obligación era tratar de hacer una lista donde ellos también estuvieran incluidos. Hemos detectado un compromiso extraordinario y la disposición de los clubes ha sido total", comentó el seleccionador. Mateo ha vuelto a llamar a jugadores de su máxima confianza como Francis Alonso, Pierre Oriola (pegamento del bueno), Oriol Paulí, Bassas, Jaime Fernández y Álex Reyes. Es el núcleo duro de la selección en este tramo de la temporada, donde aflora también la fantástica clase media alta del baloncesto español. La no presencia de Ricky Rubio y la lesión de Alberto Díaz han motivado la apuesta por otro base, Alocén, que regresa como invitado a una convocatoria dos años después tras superar sus lesiones. Se estrenarán con Chus el alero Héctor Alderete (La Laguna Tenerife), el pívot Sima (Alba Berlín), el ala-pívot Pablo Tamba (Basquet Manresa), que le da su sentido al training camp que organizó Mateo en mayo porque el andaluz estuvo allí, el alero Adriá Torres (Joventut), que jugó el Europeo sub20 y también ha formado parte de la selección sub18 de 3x3, y el alero Mikel Sanz (Lleida), que nunca ha sido internacional en ninguna categoría. Todos estos jugadores invitados serán básicos en el día a día hasta que se vayan incorporando los internacionales que compiten en Euroliga, que lo harán progresivamente a lo largo de la semana. No todos estarán disponibles en el primer partido ante Montenegro. Sí se espera en Podgorica a Juancho, Cárdenas, Saint Supery, Brizuela y Parra. La concentración arrancará el 23 de noviembre en Guadalajara y la expedición de la selección volará a Podgorica el miércoles 25. Al día siguiente (19.00 h), el equipo nacional se medirá a Montenegro. “Tengo el índice de ilusión y orgullo a tope. Vamos a sumar dos victorias, estoy seguro. Estoy orgullosa del compromiso y sentido de pertenencia de los jugadores. Cuando hay que arrimar el hombro, ahí estamos, están todos. Chus ha sido capaz de involucrar a todos los jugadores y de implementar una identidad en el juego. Nos genera seguridad. Estoy orgullosa de la afición, estamos a punto de colgar el ‘no hay billetes’ para el partido de Santiago. Todo esto nos hará acercarnos al objetivo principal: ser protagonistas en el Mundial”. Así lo resumió la presidenta Elisa Aguilar.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham has a message for the NBA after Luka Doncic incident as his offensive brilliance catches her attention
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham has backed a proposed NBA rule change that grew out of a Luka Doncic technical foul.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has backed a proposed NBA rule change that grew out of a Luka Doncic technical foul. The Lakers star was hit with the call against the Portland Trail Blazers after he threw the ball toward a referee in frustration. Trainer Drew Hanlen used the moment to argue that technicals should be wiped when officials blow the original call, and Cunningham quickly agreed. All of it came while Doncic is averaging 38.6 points a game and right after he left a win over the Bucks with an ankle injury.Why does Sophie Cunningham support the NBA rule change?Sophie Cunningham liked the idea as soon as Hanlen pitched it. He raised it on the No Hesitation podcast while laughing about the disbelief of six-time All-Star Luka Doncic at being teed up in the Portland game. Hanlen was careful to say he was not claiming the referee blew that particular call. His point was about the rule itself. If a ref misses a call and a player reacts to it, he argued, “that technical should be wiped.”Cunningham needed only four words to answer: “I agree, I agree.”The idea has a catch. Some reactions cross the line even when the whistle was wrong, and nobody wants players throwing balls at officials without consequences. Any rule change would need clear wording on what qualifies for a wipe. Without it, the league could end up with more arguments about technicals, not fewer.The moment stood out because of the zero-tolerance stance the Slovenian had taken only days earlier.Doncic’s scoring run continues with a positive ankle updateCunningham has been just as taken with the way Doncic is playing. She said on her podcast that his highlights keep filling her social media feeds, and that he has been “so much fun to watch.” She admitted it has become hard to look away.The numbers back her up. Through 11 games, Doncic is averaging 38.6 points, 7.5 rebounds and 7.6 assists while shooting 48.9% from the field and 40.8% from three. He has scored at least 30 points in nine straight games, and the Lakers are 11-2.The ankle scare came in the Bucks game. Doncic landed on Kyle Kuzma’s foot late in the fourth quarter of a 123-112 Lakers win, after putting up 32 points, five rebounds, five assists, and three steals in 32 minutes. It was the seventh straight win for Los Angeles.The early word is good. Doncic woke up Thursday with no pain in the ankle, and coach JJ Redick had called it “just a light tweak” after the game. Doncic played it down too, telling reporters, “I’ll be fine.” Lakers need Doncic in good health, as he is dominating the league.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
